claims.finding: Version selection prioritizes currently streaming/latest placeholder, then matching version UUID, tool-use ID, message UUID, and finally newest index.
The body resolver compares nonempty server records with client-rebuilt versions, carries forward repeated client bodies, and has two guarded partial-record heuristics.
claims.limit: This is client conflict selection, not evidence of the server write/merge algorithm.

claims.finding: Plain text forces raw source; Code/Markdown hide the mode switch. While current artifact is streaming, HTML/React/SVG/Mermaid cannot use normal preview. HTML/React expose refresh outside raw mode.

The code renderer uses a 500 ms comparison baseline for a streaming highlight flag, not a 500 ms source-content debounce. Update streams seek to the first differing line percentage; streaming end re-enables scrolling.

Rich rendering uses an iframe at configured userContentRendererUrl with sandbox allow-scripts/allow-same-origin, fullscreen/clipboard-write allowance, and no-referrer. Renderer query includes parentOrigin and optional parent error reporting.
claims.limit: Actual renderer origin/configuration, response headers/CSP, and renderer implementation were not obtained.

claims.finding: The communicator sends a MessageChannel handshake; window messages must match the configured origin and exact iframe contentWindow. Port messages are parsed without an origin field, after the port is transferred through that window boundary.

Both ingress paths enforce a 30-message/5-second counter excluding recognized pending responses, parse envelope and method/payload schemas, reject duplicate tracked IDs, check permission, and map handler failures to a response.

Processed-request memory holds at most 1000 IDs; IDs longer than 256 characters are not stored in the de-duplication set. Capability promises are launched after awaited permission checks rather than serially awaited to completion.
claims.limit: This bounded set is not unlimited replay prevention; separate schema limits must be evaluated independently.

claims.finding: The generic sendRequest path has no timer in the inspected implementation. A disconnected iframe early-returns within the promise executor. Cleanup closes the port, removes listeners, and clears queued messages, without visibly settling every in-flight promise.
claims.limit: This identifies a local missing completion edge, not proof that every caller hangs; individual callers may impose deadlines.

claims.finding: Content state distinguishes initial undefined, an unacked sentinel, and an acknowledged type/content object. Content posts advance the sequence and invalidate acknowledgement unless the same type/body is already acknowledged. Only a successful current-sequence response restores acknowledgement. Inbound receipts snapshot sequence and content state, including undefined; an older receipt cannot inherit a later acknowledgement.

ReadyForContent sets the renderer-ready state. SetContent is posted only after readiness and nonempty content/type, while content delivery, DOMContentLoaded, and first-paint timing are separate signals.

Capabilities require their supplied handlers and method-specific content/consent checks. GetFile, SendConversationMessage and StorageGet/Set/Delete/List reject the unacked sentinel at their content gate, not undefined. ClaudeCompletion and ProxyFetch also reject unacked and apply separate consent/account/budget logic. External open/download uses the type/content matcher. Project/shared-data permissions can involve dialogs. Capture-only instances remove capability props and proxy fetch.
claims.limit: Presence of a protocol method does not imply implementation or permission in every caller. RunCode exists in schemas but not this handler branch.

claims.finding: External opens and downloads are separately mediated, require the shown content acknowledgement and reject capture-only use. Downloads strip control/bidi/path characters from filenames. UI asks before trusted download/open flows.

Proxy fetch accepts only the configured Anthropic hostname in this branch, forwards a small header allowlist, strips selected credential response headers, uses manual redirects, and streams with a 10 MiB body ceiling. At queue flush, fetch compares artifactIdentityKey; storage compares consentKey only when shared is true. Non-shared storage invokes the captured operation without that flush-time identity rejection. A separate enqueue path can reject the existing storage queue when a newly enqueued request has a different artifact UUID; this is not unconditional identity-change cleanup.

evidence.anchor: fetch request cancelled: artifact changed while queued

claims.limit: Describes declared client dispatch; no endpoint was called and backend enforcement was not inspected.

claims.finding: Renderer error schemas distinguish unsupported imports, runtime errors, missing files, completion errors, and storage errors. Error state records artifact ID/version/posted content; content changes and refresh clear stale errors.
The local import-name list is used to classify unsupported-import errors for telemetry; it is not a recovered runtime module loader or definitive import allowlist.
claims.limit: Actual React transformation, library versions/resolution, and Mermaid compiler remain renderer-side unknowns.

claims.finding: A screenshot request requires capture-only mode, the credentialless property, and no observed private-data touch; it is bounded to 15 seconds and validates returned image size/type. Live-frame capture is deliberately rejected.

The separate Mermaid diagram component also waits for ReadyForContent before SetContent; it denies requested non-always-permitted capabilities and shows the source with an error message on rejected render.
claims.limit: This distinct transcript-diagram component must not be confused with the full artifact pane.

claims.finding: Frame workspace messages use a different same-origin chrome protocol. Version reports validate marker/state/UUID/availability, match source window and artifact UUID, and carry preview/live version state.

Embedded frame version-preview commands are accepted only when owner/writer preview support is available; the receiver checks same-origin parent or permitted opener source, validates the command, and applies a 250 ms floor.
claims.limit: This exposes an editor boundary; it does not recover a collaborative editing algorithm or server persistence guarantee.

claims.finding: Page chrome validates a versioned object containing save state, action/export descriptors, comment count, optional layout/background values, and leaveLosesWork. The host renders a save indicator and optional save-now action from this reported state.
claims.limit: A saved indicator is a reported editor state, not independent evidence of durable server storage.

claims.finding: Workspace dialog/fullscreen/minimized modes are scoped in memory; minimizing preserves the previous visible mode, and scope teardown forgets it. A switcher changes artifact keys, separately from selecting artifact version.
claims.limit: No claim that this viewer mode, complete tab arrangement, or full version history persists across process restart.

claims.finding: Chat artifact Escape closes only if relevant overlays/menus are absent; HTML comment mode consumes Escape first. Close restores the remembered trigger focus or composer fallback. Frame minimize controls also implement focus restoration.
The supplied schemas include strings for HTML, React, Mermaid, SVG, Markdown, Code and text artifact types; the chat body and sandbox split follow those tags.
claims.limit: An optional schema field is not proof that a particular renderer enables that feature.
